title: Conditions and branches
subtitle: Test a condition, then take one of two paths.
concept: Test a condition, then take one of two paths.
intuition: If you have enough money for the fare, take the bus. Otherwise, take the other path.
objectives: Turn a question into a condition
Write two paths with if and else

body.title: Turn a question into a condition
body.text: Suppose the fare is 5 and money holds the amount you have. money >= 5 asks whether you have at least 5; >= means greater than or equal to. A comparison returns True or False. Predict the result before following the program.

body.title: Write two paths with if and else
body.text: if condition: starts the path taken when the condition is true; else: starts the other path. After each colon, start a new line and indent the body by four spaces. Indentation groups statements into a branch. This test takes one branch: it cannot print both messages.

body.title: Check the exact boundary
body.text: Try 6, then 4, then exactly 5. The >= comparison includes equality, so 5 is enough. Replacing it with > would reject the exact fare. Use == to compare equality; a single = assigns a value.

formalDefinition.text: An if statement runs its indented body when the condition is true. Otherwise it runs the else body. Only one branch runs.
conditions: Keep the colon and indentation. Use = for assignment and == for equality.

derivation.text: 5 >= 5 is true, so enter the if branch.

interactiveVisual.caption: Choose an input and predict the result, then select Next step. The arrow marks the next statement to execute; the side panel shows current variables and output produced so far.
interactiveVisual.followUp: Compare 4, 5, and 6. Which lines does the arrow skip?

workedExamples.title: Enough for the fare?
workedExamples.problem: You have 5 and the fare is 5. Display the decision.
steps: 5 >= 5 is true, so enter the if branch.

workedExamples.title: The other branch
steps: Skip the if body and run the else body.

commonMistakes.correction: > excludes equality. Use >= when the exact fare is enough.

commonMistakes.claim: Both the if and else bodies run.
commonMistakes.correction: This test takes one branch. When the condition is true, it skips else.

solution: The condition is false, so enter else.

practice.problem: Display Pass for a score of at least 60 and Practice again otherwise. Test 60.

learningCheck.question: Which condition includes having exactly 5?
learningCheck.explanation: >= includes equality. A single = assigns a value.
feedback: > requires more than 5 and excludes exactly 5.
A single = assigns a value; it is not an equality test.
